title: Topological superconductivity in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure
authors: Michael Liudeng, Hrishikesh Patel, Marcel Franz, Niclas Heinsdorf
abstract: Fully gapped spin-triplet superconductors offer a natural setting for topological edge transport and Majorana excitations. Here we propose a heterostructure that interfaces altermagnetic monolayer V$_2$Se$_2$O with a conventional $s$-wave superconductor. Starting from an ab-initio description of V$_2$Se$_2$O, we construct a low-energy model of its spin-split Fermi surface and study the superconducting instability of the coupled stack. We find that the momentum-dependent exchange splitting of the altermagnet strongly favors equal-spin pairing and converts the proximity-induced order into a fully gapped $p$-wave state. Over a broad range of interface parameters, the resulting Bogoliubov-de Gennes bands carry a nonzero Chern number, and slab spectra exhibit chiral Majorana edge modes traversing the bulk gap. We further quantify the inverse proximity effect and show how the induced gap evolves across a finite multilayer stack. These results establish a route to topological triplet superconductivity by interfacing a conventional superconductor with an experimentally available altermagnetic semiconductor, and provide practical guidance for interface fabrication and experimental detection.
summary: This theoretical work proposes using an altermagnetic semiconductor interfaced with an $s$-wave superconductor to create a topological triplet superconductor. By modeling the system with a BdG Hamiltonian, the authors predict the emergence of chiral Majorana edge modes, offering a practical pathway for superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a practical theoretical route to realizing topological triplet superconductivity by engineering an interface between a conventional $s$-wave superconductor and an altermagnetic semiconductor.
main_result: The altermagnetic proximity effect converts the induced pairing into a fully gapped $p$-wave state, resulting in Bogoliubov-de Gennes bands with a non-zero Chern number and observable chiral Majorana edge modes.
method: The study employs ab-initio calculations to model the band structure of the altermagnet and uses self-consistent Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) calculations to analyze the superconducting instability across the heterostructure.
model_or_system: The system is a heterostructure comprising an altermagnetic monolayer ($	ext{V}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$) interfaced with an $s$-wave superconductor. The physics is modeled using an effective BdG Hamiltonian incorporating spin-splitting from the altermagnet and superconducting pairing terms.
key_observables: Chern number of the BdG bands, chiral Majorana edge modes, and the spatial evolution of the superconducting gap ($\Delta_l$) across the multilayer stack.
important_parameters: The degree of altermagnetic exchange splitting ($\eta$), interface polarization ($p$), and the superconducting gap amplitude ($\Delta_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the superconducting instability is dominated by low-energy states near the Fermi surface, and it explicitly models the inverse proximity effect (IPE).
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the proposed heterostructure and the resulting topological state with chiral Majorana edge modes. Other figures likely show band structures and gap profiles.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the physical model using ab-initio results for the altermagnet, then constructing the full BdG Hamiltonian for the interface, and finally calculating key topological invariants and gap profiles to confirm the predicted superconducting state.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, material-based mechanism for generating topological superconductivity using magnetism, which is highly relevant for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation components.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: (a) Schematic of the proposed altermagnet–superconductor heterostructure: mono- layer V2Se2O on top of a conventional s-wave supercondutor (gray). V2Se2O is slightly hole doped, resulting in a FS of disconnected, spin-polarized hole pockets (see Fig. 2). Through the proximity effect, fully gapped topological superconductivity is induced in the bulk of the heterostructure with chiral Majorana edge modes on the boundary.

Fig. 2: Ab-initio band structure of hole-doped monolayer V2Se2O with Néel-ordered V moments of ±1.7µB. Along the diagonals of the square Brillouin zone the bands are spin degenerate (purple). Away from the md mirror line, the bands are non-degenerate and spin-polarized (red/blue). The dashed line shows the spectrum of the fitted effective four-band model hM(k). The inset shows the FS obtained from ab initio (solid) and from the effective model (dashed lines). The pockets are fully spin polarized and there is no spin degeneracy on the FS, quenching conventional, zero-momentum singlet pairing.

Fig. 3: (a) Topological phase diagram of the altermagnet–superconductor heterostruc- ture hht(k) as a function of the spin-polarization of the interface tunneling p and the hybridization vM for ∆0 = 0.2, λR = 0.2, γ = 0.9 on a 51 × 51 k-point mesh. The star and diamond mark the parameter tuple used in (b) and (c), respectively. The dashed lines show the phase boundary between ch1 = 0 and ch1 = ±1 when the spin splitting is reduced from η = 1 to η = 0.5. There is no region with ch1 = ±2 for η = 0.5. (b) Boundary spectral weight A(ω, k2) of the five outermost layers in a 100 layer slab along a1 at vM = 0.1 and p = 0.35 (green star) with ch1 = −1 and periodic boundary conditions in the a2...

Fig. 4: Self-consistent layer-resolved singlet gap ∆l across a stack of N = 100 super- conducting layers for λR = 0.2, γ = 0.9, vM = 0.1 and p = 0.35 for different values of interlayer hopping t⊥. Solid lines show the gap profiles for η = 1.0 and µM = −0.73, while dashed lines correspond to η = 0.5 and µM = −0.82. The suppression near l = 1, the layer adjacent to the magnetic interface, and its recovery toward the bulk value illustrate the IPE. Exponential fits to the recovery tails from l = 2 into the bulk yield healing lengths from approximately one to about four superconducting layers.
